annotations.text:
This one runs. Tap the floor lamp tile in the rail and the open animation plays at the measured timings; the ✕ closes it.

Three chips: Sky (dusk / night / midday), Tiles (four tones) and Weather (all fifteen conditions). Weather drives both the cloud beside the greeting AND the field behind everything — try Midday against sunny, then pouring.

The still frame, for working on the detail layout without the animation in the way.

The field goes amber because a warm lamp is what's open. A camera would push it cool.

Why the midday tiles felt off, and what changed.

Short version: the tiles were specified in fixed colour while the field moves across the whole day, so somewhere between dusk and noon a tile stops being lighter than the sky and starts being darker. Now lightness is relative and the crossing can't happen.

Follow the light is back, doing the thing that's actually distinct: the tiles change hue family, cool and light while the sun is up, lamplit and low once it's down. Every tone tracks the sky's lightness — this one also changes character.

The extra-dim switch is a preference now, not the fix: Pastel at night lands at L 0.483 rather than 0.80 on its own.

The weather lozenge is gone from the rail — the sky behind the panel already IS the forecast, so a tile saying 'clear' repeated the whole screen.

The cloud and the 17° moved beside the greeting, where the row was one line of text across 1440px. That bought back 264px: it now holds Tonight's two scenes, and the back door.

One illustration built from parts, not fifteen drawings. It reads the same {clouds, rain, snow, fog, lightning, wind} that wxOf() already hands the sky, so the picture and the sky cannot disagree — and a new condition needs no new art.

The field takes the same three mixes palette() applies, which is why the tiles dim in heavy rain without anything special-casing rain.
